explanation: First detect an unbounded zero-weight type. Otherwise compute the best value for each capacity by considering the last positive-weight item selected.
correctness: For a bounded instance, an optimal nonempty selection has a final positive-weight item. Removing it leaves a feasible selection at the remaining capacity, so maximizing all such choices establishes the recurrence by induction.
walkthrough: For types [weight=3,value=7] and [weight=5,value=13] with capacity 11, choose one weight-5 item and two weight-3 items. Total weight is 11 and value is 13+7+7=27. Two weight-5 items yield only 26; three weight-3 items yield 21. The unbounded dynamic program reuses earlier capacity optima to find 27.
timeComplexity: O(t*C+t+C) time for t types and capacity C, including initialization and zero/empty cases.
